about: Every mutant of the recorded run that the tests did not kill, by class, with a verdict and a reason. `scripts/check_mutation_survivors.py` compares a fresh run against this file and fails on a survivor it does not name, on an entry whose mutant no longer survives, and on a class without a verdict or a reason. A class called equivalent is one where the mutant computes the same thing as the original, so no test can kill it. A class called a gap is one where a test could, and none does; the entry says what such a test would have to do.

text-not-asserted.reason: a string constant rewritten -- a heading, a word inside a message, a key of a diagnostic block, the case of a status -- where no assertion reaches it. The golden artefacts compare every line of five fixtures' six artefacts and the refusal tests compare every sentence of every refusal, so what survives is text on a path those fixtures do not enter.
text-not-asserted.what_would_kill_it: a fixture that enters the branch, compared as a golden artefact, or an assertion on the sentence that branch produces

value-not-asserted.reason: a value handed on unchanged -- a field of a returned record, an argument of a call -- replaced by None or by another constant, in a place where the number is computed but never compared with anything.
value-not-asserted.what_would_kill_it: an assertion on that field of the returned record

constant-not-asserted.reason: a numeric literal changed by one: an index, a gate, a bound. Where the constant is a gate, tests/test_degenerate_shapes.py now stands on several of them; what survives is a gate no fixture reaches exactly.
constant-not-asserted.what_would_kill_it: an input that sits exactly on the gate the constant sets

argument-dropped.reason: a keyword or positional argument removed from a call: `nrows=`, `stacklevel=`, `errors='raise'`, a field of a constructor. Some members are unobservable by construction -- `stacklevel` changes only which line a warning is attributed to -- and the class is called a gap because that cannot be shown for each member without reading it.
argument-dropped.what_would_kill_it: an assertion on the behaviour the argument buys

boundary-comparison.reason: `<` became `<=` or the reverse. The two differ only on an input that sits exactly on the bound. The degenerate-shape battery puts a fixture on several of those bounds; what survives is a bound no fixture reaches exactly, and for some of them no admissible input can.
boundary-comparison.what_would_kill_it: a cohort whose value falls exactly on the bound

dtype-inferred-instead-of-declared.reason: a declared dtype dropped (`dtype=float`, `dtype=object`, `dtype=bool`, an integer dtype, or an `astype` target), so numpy infers one. The inferred dtype agrees for the values the tests feed; integer input, a label column of mixed types, or a count large enough to overflow, would separate them.
dtype-inferred-instead-of-declared.what_would_kill_it: a fixture whose labels are not all strings, or whose counts do not fit the inferred integer type

dtype-default-is-the-same.reason: `dtype=float` dropped from `np.zeros`, `np.ones`, `np.empty` or `np.full` with a float fill, whose default is already float64, so the mutant is the same program. No test can distinguish it, and the declaration stays because it states at the point of the call what the array is for.

branch-forced.reason: a guard rewritten to `(C) and False` or `(C) or True`, which takes the branch the fixtures never take.
branch-forced.what_would_kill_it: an input for which the guard takes the other branch

warning-state.reason: an argument of `np.errstate` changed. It decides whether numpy emits a warning for an overflow, an underflow or a division, never what it computes; every number the package writes is identical under the mutant. A suite that turned warnings into errors would see the warning, which is not the same as seeing a wrong result.

logical-operator.reason: `and` became `or`, or `&` became `|`, where the operands are equal or where only one of them varies in the fixtures.
logical-operator.what_would_kill_it: an input that makes the two operands differ

arithmetic-operator.reason: an arithmetic operator changed in an expression whose value no assertion reaches, or whose operands make the two operators agree.
arithmetic-operator.what_would_kill_it: an assertion on the value of that expression

unsorted.reason: a single edit this classification could not name: a few `==`/`!=` flips, which are not equivalent. These are not reviewed one by one.
unsorted.what_would_kill_it: reading them one by one, which nobody has done

stable-sort.reason: `kind='stable'` dropped, which changes the order of tied keys and so the order of a floating-point summation. The package sorts there so that a reported figure does not move by a unit in the last place when the lineages are renamed; the metamorphic relabelling test compares to a relative 1e-9 and does not see the last bit.
stable-sort.what_would_kill_it: a bit-exact relabelling assertion on a cohort with tied contributions

control-flow.reason: `continue` became `break` or the reverse, inside a loop whose remaining iterations the fixtures make empty.
control-flow.what_would_kill_it: a fixture in which the loop has work left after the branch
